moduleTitle: Advanced Use Cases - Additional Appium Capabilities
learningObjectives: Interpret how to use additional Appium capabilities to extend mobile automation functionality.
Group capabilities by what they actually control: session lifecycle, app state, input, and dialog handling.
Recognise the visibility cost that dialog-suppressing capabilities carry.
Decide which capabilities belong in a reusable Capability Set and which belong to one TestCase.

elements.description: Appium capabilities are supplied when a session starts and cannot be changed during that session’s lifecycle. Driver-supported Settings APIs can change some runtime behavior without changing the session capabilities; distinguish those mechanisms. Tosca scan capability sets and execution Set/Add Desired Capabilities Modules are separate configuration paths.

elements.text: Standard W3C capabilities such as platformName and browserName do not need the Appium extension prefix. Appium-specific capabilities use appium: (or supported appium:options grouping). Verify the actual driver/version’s capability support rather than treating all names as universal.

bulletPoints: Session capabilities are immutable; supported runtime Settings are distinct.
Check standard versus extension names and driver/platform support.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Grouping them by what they control

elements.title: Four practical groups
items: Permissions/alerts: UiAutomator2 autoGrantPermissions has Android target SDK/API requirements and special-permission limitations. XCUITest autoAcceptAlerts is an iOS capability including privacy permission alerts; neither is a universal cross-platform popup switch.

App state: noReset/fullReset interpretation depends on the driver and application. Validate the supported combination and actual state; do not equate it with the Mobile Scan Reset application checkbox or complete backend cleanup.
Session lifetime: inspect the documented timeout for the installed driver/server; different timeouts cover different operations.
Input: XCUITest maxTypingFrequency can tune typing; other keyboard options have platform/simulator scope. Do not assume one input capability fixes every focus or locator error.

elements.description: Grouping helps navigate documentation, but a symptom does not prove one capability is the cause. Inspect the target, focus, application state and driver logs before selecting a supported change.

bulletPoints: Scope capabilities to their driver, platform and documented requirements.
Use grouping as a search aid, not a universal root-cause classifier.

elements.text: Automatically accepting alerts or granting permissions can reduce deliberate coverage of their appearance, text and acceptance/denial paths. It does not prove that every alert becomes impossible to observe in logs or other instrumentation, nor guarantee uninterrupted execution.

elements.term: Choose configuration for the test objective
elements.description: For a workflow that needs granted permissions, a supported automatic grant may be appropriate. For permission or alert behavior coverage, use controlled initial state and explicitly verify the required dialogs and outcomes. Suppression is not a universal recommended default for the whole suite.

elements.text: Treat this as independent coverage guidance. Verify which behavior was exercised, rather than treating a higher pass rate as proof of equivalent coverage.

bulletPoints: Automatic dialog handling can reduce deliberate coverage; observation is not universally impossible.
Configure controlled dialog tests for the actual required acceptance and denial paths.

elements.term: Naming a bundle you will reuse
elements.description: In the scan Capabilities window, Add capabilities set creates a named group and Add capability adds an entry to the selected group; it is not a separate ungrouped one-session mode. For execution, place Set Desired Capabilities first, with ActionMode Select, before Open Mobile App/OpenUrl; Add Desired Capabilities can extend the pending values before opening.

elements.text: Tosca documents capability carry-over between sequential TestCases: use Set Desired Capabilities first in each TestCase, leaving Name/Value blank when none are needed, to prevent unintended carry-over. Validate execution setup separately from scan configuration.

bulletPoints: Scan sets contain entries; execution uses its documented Set/Add workflow.
Prevent unintended sequential carry-over with explicit per-TestCase Set Desired Capabilities.

examPitfalls.title: Enabling dialog suppression suite-wide with no exception
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Applying autoGrantPermissions and autoAcceptAlerts everywhere, leaving no TestCase that exercises the permission or alert flow.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Choose dialog handling for the test objective; controlled initial state and explicit assertions are needed for permission/alert coverage. Automatic handling is not a universal default.

examPitfalls.title: Toggling capabilities mid-TestCase
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting a capability change to take effect partway through a running session.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Session capabilities cannot be changed after creation. Driver-supported runtime Settings are a different mechanism; configure Tosca Set/Add capabilities before the opening step.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming scan sets automatically define execution
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reusing a scan setup without checking execution capability carry-over.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Add capability belongs to the selected scan set. Validate execution Set/Add Desired Capabilities and explicit clearing for sequential tests separately.

practiceQuiz.scenario: At what point are Desired Capabilities applied?

options.text: When the automation session is created, so they apply to everything in that session.
Only when the application is installed.
After the TestCase completes, during teardown.

practiceQuiz.hint: Session capabilities and mutable driver-supported Settings are different mechanisms.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Capabilities configure the new session and are immutable during it. Some drivers expose separate runtime Settings; those do not mutate the session capabilities.

optionExplanations.A: Capabilities are not automatically renegotiated before every TestStep.
optionExplanations.B: Capabilities are supplied at session creation.
optionExplanations.C: They configure more than installation alone.
optionExplanations.D: They must configure the session before its actions, not only teardown.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An XCUITest iOS suite auto-accepts alerts and has no explicit alert assertions. Which deliberate coverage may be reduced?

options.text: Nothing; alerts are irrelevant to functional coverage.
Verification of alert text and required accept/deny interaction paths.
The application can no longer be installed by TMA.

practiceQuiz.hint: Automatic acceptance is not equivalent to explicitly testing the dialog behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Automatic acceptance can bypass deliberate text and accept/deny checks. It does not prove alerts cannot be observed through logs or other instrumentation; add objective-specific controlled tests.

optionExplanations.A: Alert behavior can be relevant to functional coverage.
optionExplanations.B: Automatic acceptance does not replace explicit text or accept/deny assertions.
optionExplanations.C: This capability does not itself disable text-entry assertions.
optionExplanations.D: Automatic alert acceptance does not prohibit application installation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Logs and inspection confirm an XCUITest typing-speed issue, with the correct target and focus. Which capability category contains maxTypingFrequency for investigation?
practiceQuiz.hint: The scenario establishes typing behavior after checking the target and focus.
practiceQuiz.rationale: XCUITest documents maxTypingFrequency for typing/clear frequency. Inspect driver/version requirements; a generic text-entry failure alone would not prove a capability cause.

optionExplanations.A: The established typing-speed issue is not a session-idle timeout diagnosis.
optionExplanations.B: The scenario does not establish reset-state failure.
optionExplanations.C: maxTypingFrequency is a documented XCUITest typing capability.
optionExplanations.D: The scenario does not establish an alert/permission obstruction.

quickRecap.value: Capabilities are set at session creation and immutable; supported runtime Settings are distinct.
Group by behavior while checking driver, platform and version requirements.
Automatic dialog handling can reduce deliberate coverage; it does not guarantee observation is impossible.
Add capability adds an entry to the selected named scan set, not an ungrouped one-off session.
Use execution Set/Add Desired Capabilities before opening and explicit Set clearing to avoid sequential carry-over.
